t: What MongoDB Engine Is All About
title: What MongoDB Engine Is All About
description: The document database: BSON documents, replica sets, sharding, aggregation pipelines.. This database covers MongoDB Engine with full records: definitions, key facts, working procedures, and runnable demo programs, arranged on a teaching ladder from Foundations to Advanced. Every database engine makes the same fundamental tradeoffs between read speed, write speed, and space amplification.
definition: MongoDB Engine — The document database: BSON documents, replica sets, sharding, aggregation pipelines.
key_points: Every database engine makes the same fundamental tradeoffs between read speed, write speed, and space amplification.
The storage engine determines the ceiling; the SQL layer determines the ergonomics.
MVCC lets readers proceed without blocking writers, which is why modern OLTP scales.
Write-ahead logging is non-negotiable for durability; every serious engine has one.
how_it_works: Define the workload first: OLTP, OLAP, or mixed; the engine choice follows the workload.
Provision with headroom: size RAM for the working set, disk for 3x data, CPU for peaks.
Enable the fundamentals: WAL archiving, automated backups, and monitoring before loading data.
Load a representative dataset and run your actual queries, not synthetic benchmarks.
Read EXPLAIN plans for the top queries; fix missing indexes and bad estimates.
Tune memory: buffer pool, work memory, and maintenance memory for your hardware.
Set up replication and test failover; measure lag under load.
Harden security: SCRAM/auth, TLS, least-privilege roles, and encryption at rest.

title: Document model
description: Document model. MongoDB stores BSON documents — JSON-like with rich types like ObjectId, Date, and Decimal128. Documents in a collection need no fixed schema; fields vary per document. The 16 MB document limit bounds single-document size.

title: WiredTiger storage
description: WiredTiger storage. WiredTiger is the default storage engine: LSM-ish B-tree with document-level locking. Compression (snappy/zlib/zstd) and checkpoints give crash safety. The cache (default 50% RAM minus 1 GB) is the hot working set.
